Three things in that table are worth stating explicitly. First, the
\emph{windowed} model's skill over offline interpolation does not survive the
shift: $-0.001$ to $+0.091$, with the CI above zero on 2/4 (cut) and 0/4
(inclusive) initialisations, and 0/4 against the causal GP. Second, its named repair works: standardizing each discharge's fast
diagnostics by \emph{its own} mean and variance at load time (targets untouched)
takes the cut-population gate from 2/4 to 4/4, paired $+0.078$, $+0.018$,
$+0.095$, $+0.049$ (3/4 significant), and leaves \Vrot{} unchanged
($-0.003$ to $+0.008$)---the expected negative control, since the \Vrot{} head
never sees the fast diagnostics. Third, and this is the result of the section:
\textbf{the sequence nowcaster does not collapse}. Its skill over PCHIP is $+0.17$
to $+0.20$ with the CI above zero on 4/4 initialisations in both populations, its
skill over the causal GP $+0.11$ to $+0.16$ (CI above zero on 4/4 in both), and its
paired skill over the windowed control $+0.09$ to $+0.18$ (CI above zero on 8/8); its
\Vrot{} skill over persistence is $+0.31$ to $+0.34$ with the CI above zero on 4/4
in both populations where the windowed control's interval includes zero on 4/4, and
its \Vrot{} margin over the control is $+0.06$ to $+0.18$ with the CI above zero on
8/8.

\paragraph{Why the control degrades---measured, not asserted.}
Between the train and test periods the median location shift, in the units the
control was normalized in, is \textbf{1.22\,$\sigma$ for BES} and
\textbf{0.53\,$\sigma$ for ECEI} (scale ratios $0.75$ and $0.62$) against
\textbf{0.115\,$\sigma$} (scale ratio $1.06$) for the CES targets, a 5--11$\times$
larger drift, so train-file-only normalization does not transfer across the campaign
boundary while per-shot standardization, which \seqv{} uses by definition and which
reads only that discharge's own data, does.

\paragraph{Two stress tests, one reading.}
The skill
over the baselines a real-time system can actually run survives both stress tests
in both populations with CIs above zero ($+0.28$ to $+0.44$ over persistence under
reweighting, $+0.11$ to $+0.16$ over the causal GP under the campaign split). The
skill over \emph{future-using} interpolation survives the temporal shift in both
populations ($+0.17$ to $+0.20$, CIs above zero) and the MNAR reweighting with
population-conditional significance ($+0.14$ to $+0.28$, CI above zero on 2/4 cut
and 4/4 inclusive).

\subsection{The \Ti$\leftrightarrow$\Vrot{} information asymmetry}
\label{sec:asym}
A controlled input-modality ablation on the windowed control---one modality group
zeroed \emph{at evaluation}, no retraining, persistence and interpolants computed
from the real history---explains \emph{why} the two targets behave differently and
re-grounds the routing of \S\ref{sec:model} under the confirmed protocol
(Table~\ref{tab:ablation}).

\begin{table}[t]
  \centering
  \caption{Evaluation-time modality ablation of the $W{=}2$ windowed control,
  TEST, both populations: $\skillp$ (4-split mean) and the paired change against
  the un-ablated run (splits 42 / 1 / 7 / 123; $^{*}$ = significantly worse).}
  \label{tab:ablation}
  \small
  \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
  \begin{tabular}{llcc}
    \toprule
    Inputs & target & cut & inclusive \\
    \midrule
    Full (history + fast + time) & \Ti{} & $+0.173$ & $+0.238$ \\
    History + time only (\emph{no fast}) & \Ti{} & $-0.125$; paired $-0.25^{*}$ / $-0.38^{*}$ / $-0.42^{*}$ / $-0.43^{*}$ & $+0.201$; paired $-0.03^{*}$ / $-0.04$ / $-0.03$ / $-0.09^{*}$ \\
    Fast + time only (\emph{no history}) & \Ti{} & $-2.11$; paired $-4.6^{*}$ / $-1.8^{*}$ / $-2.3^{*}$ / $-1.9^{*}$ & $-1.16$; paired $-1.5^{*}$ / $-3.4^{*}$ / $-1.2^{*}$ / $-1.1^{*}$ \\
    \midrule
    Full & \Vrot{} & $+0.213$ & $+0.206$ \\
    History + time only (\emph{no fast}) & \Vrot{} & $+0.213$; paired $+0.000$ $\times 4$ (\textbf{bit-identical}) & $+0.206$; paired $+0.000$ $\times 4$ (\textbf{bit-identical}) \\
    Fast + time only (\emph{no history}) & \Vrot{} & $-2.89$; paired $-5.4^{*}$ / $-6.3^{*}$ / $-1.8^{*}$ / $-2.3^{*}$ & $-3.51$; paired $-6.9^{*}$ / $-7.8^{*}$ / $-1.9^{*}$ / $-2.2^{*}$ \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}}
\end{table}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{History is indispensable for both targets.} Without the CES
        history the windowed model falls to $-1$ to $-4$ against PCHIP on both
        targets in both populations: neither target is predictable from 100\,Hz
        diagnostics without its own anchor.
  \item \textbf{\Ti{}: the margin over interpolation is fast-diagnostic
        information---in the cut population.} With BES/ECEI/MC zeroed the
        control drops \emph{below} the interpolator ($-0.10$ to $-0.18$; paired
        $-0.25$ to $-0.43$, 4/4 significant). The physical channel is collisional
        electron--ion coupling ($t_{ei}\propto T_e^{3/2}/n_e$): ECEI supplies $T_e$
        and BES supplies $n_e$ structure.
  \item \textbf{In the inclusive population the same history-only model still
        has skill $+0.15$ to $+0.23$ over PCHIP}, and the fast channels add only
        $0.03$--$0.09$ (2/4 significant): the interpolant's anchors are spiked and a
        learned model discounts them where an interpolant cannot. The
        spike-inclusive margin therefore contains a \emph{spike-robustness}
        component that is not fast-diagnostic information, which is the measured
        reason this paper reports two populations rather than the more flattering
        one alone; the cut population is the one that isolates what the fast
        diagnostics contribute.
  \item \textbf{\Vrot{}: information is entirely CES history, by construction and
        by measurement.} Zeroing the fast diagnostics leaves the \Vrot{} output
        \emph{bit-identical} on 8/8 population--split cells (the routing is
        structural), and \seqv{}'s and \bthree{}'s \Vrot{} branches pass the same
        perturbation test; since the routing is structural, the measurement behind
        it is the term-by-term audit of \S\ref{sec:model:physics}. Toroidal rotation
        is driven by momentum sources none of our inputs observe---the external NBI
        torque and intrinsic rotation drives~\citep{Rice2007IntermachineComparison}.
        The NBI torque, a step input, sets the level rather than the 10\,ms
        increment: the band carried by a 300\,ms moving average holds 0.34\% of the
        10\,ms \Vrot{} increment variance (\S\ref{sec:headroom}). The Mirnov signals are
        sampled at 100\,Hz, aliasing away the kHz mode-rotation frequencies that
        could otherwise proxy rotation (\S\ref{sec:headroom}).
\end{itemize}

This asymmetry was predicted from physics before the ablation and is confirmed by
it. The \Vrot{} gain over interpolation is carried by the CES history alone, and
under the registered two-level bootstrap that gain has the interval
$[+0.07, +0.70]$ over PCHIP (cut), excluding zero (Table~\ref{tab:replicate}); in
the median the physics filter's error ratio to persistence includes 1 at the 10\,ms
photon floor (\S\ref{sec:physfilter}). The fast-diagnostic null is a finding about diagnostic information content, not a model
failure. It also motivates the per-target routing of \S\ref{sec:model}. The
statement is scoped: it holds for standard CES at 10\,ms, from the core to the
pedestal top, with the NBI torque unobserved. Edge $E_r$ and edge rotation are known
to move within an ELM cycle at sub-millisecond
resolution~\citep{Viezzer2020Dynamics,Cavedon2017Pedestal}, which a 10\,ms
single-sightline exposure does not resolve, so nothing here speaks to the edge inside
an ELM cycle.

\subsection{What does the complexity buy, and does size help? A ladder and a
width sweep}
\label{sec:ladder}

The model-size and model-family axes are closed; each was measured under the same
protocol with its decision rule fixed before TEST scoring. The interpretable rung
\bthree{} (\S\ref{sec:model:rung}; 21{,}498 parameters) has a paired \Ti{} skill
against the backbone of $-0.009$, $-0.005$, $+0.026$, $-0.004$ in the cut population
(mean $+0.002$, every CI containing zero) and of $-0.16$ to $-0.21$ in the inclusive
one (mean $-0.194$, CI below zero on 4/4 splits), where a bounded correction cannot
recover a spiked carried value: rows whose persistence error exceeds 2\,keV are
0.6--1.3\% of the inclusive test rows and carry 73--83\% of \bthree{}'s \Ti{} squared
error (70--83\% of every other arm's, PCHIP included). Widening the \seqv{} \Ti{}
encoder from 24 to 260 units (34k / 49k / 114k / 358k / 879k parameters, a 26$\times$
range) gives mean \Ti{} skill $+0.230$ / $+0.236$ / $+0.235$ / $+0.236$ / $+0.230$
(cut), within $\pm 0.008$ of the 358k backbone on average, with \Vrot{} unchanged
($+0.250$ to $+0.254$). Averaging four initializations changes \Ti{} skill by a paired
$+0.020$ in the cut population (CI above zero on 4/4 splits) and $+0.007$ in the
inclusive one (2/4), on the pre-registered 0.02 band and not above it. In an offline
model-family card (gap-filling, scored against a bidirectional version of the backbone), a
shot-encoding neural process and a transformer pretrained on another tokamak (and the
same transformer from a random initialization) change \Ti{} skill by $-0.094$ to
$+0.026$, no arm clearing the 0.02 band in both populations, and with no same-shot
\Vrot{} label every arm's skill against the training mean is $-0.003$ to $-0.040$.

\subsection{The edge concentrates in high-variability neighbourhoods}
\label{sec:peak}
Using a target-independent, input-side proxy for local activity (large
neighbour-bracket slope and/or high local CES-neighbour variance, computed
\emph{excluding} the target row), we split each TEST split into ``peak''
(high-local-activity; 4.1--4.6k \Ti{} rows and 2.4--2.9k \Vrot{} rows per split) and
bulk rows and score \seqv{} in each with the shot-clustered bootstrap
(Fig.~\ref{fig:peak}):

\begin{itemize}
  \item \Ti{}: peak-stratum $\skillp = +0.45$ to $+0.61$ (cut) and $+0.62$ to
        $+0.72$ (inclusive), \textbf{PASS on 8/8}, against an interpolator that
        has the future neighbour; the bulk carries $+0.09$ to $+0.20$ (cut, PASS
        4/4) and $+0.06$ to $+0.19$ (inclusive, PASS 2/4). Interpolation is
        near-optimal on the smooth bulk; the model's value is in the active
        stretches, and that statement is unconditional.
  \item \Vrot{}: peak-stratum skill $+0.54$ to $+0.79$ (point estimates positive
        on 8/8, PASS 2/4 in each population, against persistence $+0.75$ to
        $+0.86$ PASS 8/8), and $\approx 0$ in the bulk ($-0.07$ to $+0.15$, PASS
        0/8). The asymmetry is therefore \emph{regional}: on the four-split
        count the global \Vrot{} interval vs.\ interpolation includes zero on 3/4
        and 2/4 splits (the replicate's pooled readout later puts the mean skill
        above zero, \S\ref{sec:headline}), but in high-activity
        neighbourhoods---where smooth
        past+future interpolation is worst---even the history-driven \Vrot{}
        predictor adds value. We report it as a regional strength with a thin
        significance base, not as the basis of the global claim, which rests on the replicate (\S\ref{sec:headline}).
\end{itemize}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.9\linewidth]{fig_peak}
  \caption{Peak-stratified TEST skill of \seqv{}, both populations (4-split means,
  per-split points, PR4 counts). The skill over interpolation concentrates
  where interpolation is weakest; \Vrot{} skill lives entirely in the peak stratum.}
  \label{fig:peak}
\end{figure}

\subsection{The aggregate skill is a tail effect: in the median row the nowcaster carries its anchor}
\label{sec:bulk}

An MSE-based skill is decided by a sum of squared errors, and that sum is decided by
a few large ones: the backbone's top 1\% of \Ti{} squared-error rows carry 48\% (cut)
and 83\% (inclusive) of the total (PCHIP: 51\% and 87\%). ``$+0.24$ on \Ti{}'' is
therefore not, by itself, a statement that the model's error is below interpolation's on a
\emph{typical} row. To separate the two we re-scored the frozen TEST artifacts, with
no retraining, under three robust co-metrics whose rules---and the sentence each
outcome would write---were fixed before any number: a median-absolute-error skill
$M_1 = 1 - \mathrm{medAE}_{\text{model}}/\mathrm{medAE}_{\text{PCHIP}}$
(shot-clustered weighted-median bootstrap), the skill of a Huber loss clipped at the
target's own 10\,ms reproducibility bound (\Ti{} 129.9\,eV, \Vrot{} 16.4\,km/s),
$M_2$, and a symmetric 1\%-trimmed MSE skill $M_3$.

\paragraph{The \Ti{} advantage comes from the tail.} $M_1$ against PCHIP is negative,
and significantly so, on all 16 population $\times$ target $\times$ split cells (cut
\Ti{} $-0.198$, inclusive $-0.562$). On half of the rows the model's error is at or above PCHIP's (win rate
0.48); the quantile ladder of the error ratio model/PCHIP falls from 1.20 at q50
through 1.01 at q70 and 0.96 at q75 to 0.78 at q99---the ratio drops below 1 in the upper
error quartile, the fit-failure, transient and ELM rows. In that tail $M_2$
($+0.156$) and $M_3$ ($+0.210$) are both significantly positive, so it is not an
effect of the top 1\% alone. The median row has a simpler picture: the backbone's
47\,eV is persistence's 46\,eV and the target's own bulk scatter of 46.4\,eV.
\emph{On a typical row the nowcaster carries the last observation, noise included},
and PCHIP is 20\% better there because averaging with the future neighbour halves
that noise---a gain no causal method can have. The bulk ordering (acausal GP 38.5
$<$ PCHIP 39.4 $<$ causal GP 44.4 $<$ persistence 46.1 $\approx$ backbone 47.2) is
exactly the ordering of how many noisy samples each method averages.

\paragraph{The backbone's \Vrot{} median deficit is not a tail artifact.} The pre-registration wrote
``ties in aggregate but wins in the median'' down as \Vrot{}'s possible rescue. The
opposite was observed: $M_1 = -0.488$ (cut) and $-0.518$ (inclusive), significantly
negative on 4/4 splits, and in the median row the model is worse than persistence
(4.3 vs 3.7\,km/s). The backbone's aggregate skill is a bulk deficit offset by a
tail gain (peak-stratum $+0.54$ to $+0.79$, \S\ref{sec:peak}), the same conclusion as
the term-by-term audit of \S\ref{sec:model:physics}. The \Vrot{} mean is therefore read from
the backbone (two-level interval excluding zero, Table~\ref{tab:replicate}) and the
median from the physics filter (\S\ref{sec:physfilter}).

\paragraph{The loss's influence function moves that bulk.} One variable was
changed---the influence function of the training loss---with the residual scale
$\delta$ pinned to the target's own 10\,ms reproducibility bound (cut: \Ti{}
129.9\,eV, \Vrot{} 16.4\,km/s; inclusive 274.3\,eV): a Huber loss ($r^2$ inside,
$2\delta|r|-\delta^2$ outside), everything else the backbone's. Selected on its own
validation objective, the Huber arm's \Ti{} median-AE skill against the MSE backbone
is $M_1 = +0.128$ $[+0.114, +0.141]$ in the cut population (CI above zero on 4/4
splits) at a pooled MSE difference of $+0.007$ with the interval including zero
(significant deficits 0/4), with the \Ti{} median at 0.894$\times$ persistence; in the
inclusive population $M_1 = +0.285$ $[+0.250, +0.322]$ (4/4) but one split keeps a
\Ti{} MSE difference of $-0.040$ with the CI below zero (unchanged when the epoch cap
is raised from 60 to 100), so by the pre-registered rule the Huber arm is the
\textbf{robust rung, conditional on the cut population}, and the backbone keeps the
MSE loss. The Huber rows of Table~\ref{tab:bulk} are the same loss selected on
validation MSE, which lowers the cut-population median by 8--10\% (\Ti{} 47.2 to
43.4\,eV, \Vrot{} 4.3 to 3.8\,km/s) at a paired MSE skill of $-0.004$ / $-0.007$ with
the interval including zero.

\subsection{A physics filter is the median estimator: a dual readout}
\label{sec:physfilter}

\S\ref{sec:bulk} located the headroom in the median row, where the backbone only
equals persistence. That row is the regime a filter is built for: a slowly varying
level observed through noise, with occasional jumps. We therefore asked whether a
\emph{physical} measurement model, not a learned one, owns the median. The cell is a
scalar state-space filter per target, run causally on the CES history alone: the
prior holds the level and lets it jump at rate $\lambda$ with jump variance
$\sigma_J^2$, and the measurement is Student-$t$ ($\nu_0 = 3$) at the target's
10\,ms bulk scatter estimated on TRAIN (\Ti{} 0.116 / 0.071 target s.d.\ in the cut /
inclusive population, \Vrot{} 0.060). Every parameter is fixed by the registration;
training it end-to-end moves none of them by more than 7\%, so they are not reported
as measured plasma quantities.
With Student-$t$ noise at that bulk scale the pure filter's median absolute error is
\textbf{0.916$\times$ / 0.911$\times$} persistence for \Ti{} and
\textbf{0.975$\times$ / 0.976$\times$} for \Vrot{} (cut / inclusive).

\paragraph{One output cannot carry both objectives.} Adding the backbone's
MSE-trained residual to the filter ($y = a + r$) meets the physics-rung bar in the
cut population ($M_1$ vs the backbone $+0.077$ to $+0.117$, 4/4, MSE deficit
$\le 1/4$) and misses the inclusive MSE guard by 0.0014, and in each of the three
registered variants---the plain residual, its checkpoint selected on validation
median error, and the residual weighted by the filter's variance gain---the combined
output gives the filter's median back (\Vrot{} 1.07--1.21$\times$ persistence), so
within this family an output that must also hold the aggregate moves the quiet rows.

\paragraph{The dual readout.} The pre-registered consequence is to report the median
and the mean from separate estimators on the same rows (Table~\ref{tab:dual}). For
\Ti{} the physics filter is the median estimator \textbf{unconditionally}: its median
skill is $+0.06$ to $+0.39$ over the backbone and $+0.08$ to $+0.09$ over persistence,
CIs above zero on 4/4 splits in both populations, at 0.906--0.920$\times$
persistence with a split spread of $\pm0.007$, against $\pm0.1$ or more for every
trained arm. For \Vrot{} its median skill over the backbone is $+0.09$ to $+0.27$ with
CIs above zero on 4/4 splits in both populations, and its median-error ratio to
persistence is 0.94--1.00$\times$ by split with the interval including 1 on 3/4 splits.
That interval still includes 1 after fitting the filter on TRAIN. Likelihood-fitted jump statistics
(5--13\,Hz) and a likelihood-fitted noise law (Student-$t$ with $\nu\to2$ and a
2.2\,km\,s$^{-1}$ core) leave the median at 0.97--0.98$\times$ persistence, with
the interval excluding 1 on at most 2/4 splits. The reason is measured. The 10\,ms scatter
sits at the photon floor: the ratio of the relative \Ti{} scatter to the Doppler
velocity scatter is the $\sqrt2$ of a Gaussian line fit in 8/8 split--population
cells, and the noise of the two channels is independent. Between labels the filter's
predictive is symmetric about the carried value, so its median-optimal point is the
last value. The included-1 interval is therefore a limit of the 10\,ms CES measurement, not of the
estimator. The
filter's aggregate MSE skill against the backbone is $-0.06$ to $-0.52$ because event
rows stay late, which is exactly why it is not the mean estimator. The deployment
statement becomes: median from the filter, mean from the nowcaster, and the trade
between them measured, not hidden in one output.

\subsection{The predictive distribution: one heavy-tailed peak, reported calibrated}
\label{sec:dist}

A nowcast used for control needs an uncertainty, so the backbone's head was replaced
by a predictive distribution trained by its negative log-likelihood (nothing else
changes; the posterior mean goes through the same point harness). Three likelihood
families were registered in turn: a heteroscedastic Gaussian, a two-component
Gaussian mixture, and a Student-$t$ with learnable $\nu$. The reference is the
backbone's point prediction with its own TEST RMSE as the scale, an oracle choice
that favours the reference. The registration fixed four guards (CRPS gain, central
50\,\% and 90\,\% coverage, and no posterior-mean MSE loss against the backbone)
and named the arm before any number.

\paragraph{The Gaussian is rejected.} Its central 50\,\% interval covers 0.62--0.80
of the rows (Fig.~\ref{fig:pit}): a single Gaussian scale inflated by the tail rows
is too wide for the bulk. On \Vrot{} its likelihood weighting is pulled by the
$|v| > 1000$\,km\,s$^{-1}$ fit failures and its mean's MSE skill against the backbone
is $-0.03$ to $-0.09$, with the CI below zero on 3/4 cut splits.

\paragraph{The named arms are calibrated.} In the cut population the Student-$t$ head's
CRPS difference to the mixture is $+0.009$, inside the 0.02 tie width, and it is named for
having fewer parameters. Its CRPS gain over the reference is $+0.229$ (\Ti{}) and
$+0.363$ (\Vrot{}), with the CI above zero on every split, with 50\,\% / 90\,\% coverage
0.48--0.51 / 0.91--0.92. In the inclusive population only the mixture passes the
guards ($+0.444$ / $+0.351$, coverage 0.53--0.55 / 0.90--0.91). The $t$ location
there is a redescending estimator: on the $>3$\,keV fit-failure rows it stays at the
bulk and pays their full square in MSE ($-0.134$ on the peak rows), whereas the
mixture moves its mean with the wide component.

\paragraph{What the distribution says about the physics.} The mixture never uses two
peaks: its two-mode test fires on no row, and the second component is a wide one
with weight $\approx 0.07$. The fitted $t$ tail is $\nu = 2.8$--$3.5$ for \Ti{} and
sits on the $\nu > 2$ floor for \Vrot{}. The nowcast error is therefore one
heavy-tailed peak: a narrow photon-noise core with rare large departures from events
and fit failures, the same shape the physics filter needed for its measurement model
(\S\ref{sec:physfilter}). The \Ti{} predictive width rises 1.2$\times$ on event rows;
the \Vrot{} width does not grow with the time since the last label, so the \Vrot{}
uncertainty is a per-discharge scale, not a variance that accumulates between
labels. Figure~\ref{fig:interval} shows the intervals on one held-out discharge.

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.98\linewidth]{fig_pit}
  \caption{PIT histograms on the frozen TEST rows, four splits pooled. Filled: the
  registered arm (Student-$t$ in the cut population, mixture in the inclusive one).
  Outline: the Gaussian head. A flat histogram at density 1 is calibrated; a central
  hump means intervals that are too wide in the bulk.}
  \label{fig:pit}
\end{figure}

\begin{figure}[t]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.98\linewidth]{fig_interval}
  \caption{Posterior mean and central 50\,\% / 90\,\% predictive intervals of the
  Student-$t$ head on the held-out discharge \#31815 (split 42, cut population),
  with the CES measurements. The \Ti{} axis is cut at 0; the first row's interval
  extends below it.}
  \label{fig:interval}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Cut-threshold sensitivity}
\label{sec:cutsens}
Retraining the backbone with the spike threshold at 2.5 and 4\,keV (four splits
each, scored in its own population) gives mean \Ti{} skill $+0.230$ and $+0.232$
against $+0.236$ at 3\,keV, PR4 4/4 vs.\ PCHIP and 4/4 vs.\ the causal GP at every
threshold, and \Vrot{} $+0.252$ / $+0.253$ / $+0.257$. The threshold is
immaterial across the range a physicist would defend; what matters is the two
populations, not where inside the tail the cut falls.

\subsection{Context, structure and cost: what sets skill and what sets the price}
\label{sec:context}

History length, contiguous context, operator family and cost were moved separately,
each under a pre-registered rule. In the windowed family a 24-run sweep
($W \in \{2,3,4,6,8\}$ and a history-0 point, four split seeds each; hold-free,
per-file cap 500, inclusive population) puts the mean \Ti{} skill at $-0.026$ (PR4
0/4) and \Vrot{} at $-0.78$ with no past CES observation, at $+0.238$ (4/4) and
$+0.206$ with one, and at $+0.190$ to $+0.246$ and $+0.190$ to $+0.206$ for every
longer window, against a seed spread of $0.07$--$0.16$ within a single point, so the
smallest-$W$-at-plateau rule returns $W = 2$. For the backbone, trained at each
context length $r$ on non-overlapping segments (truncating a trained state after the
fact reads unlearned state reconstruction as missing information; retraining recovers
at least 84\% of that deficit), the pre-registered rule---the smallest $r$ whose
deficit against full context is under 0.02 with at most one significant deficit out
of four splits---returns \textbf{5 steps $=$ 50\,ms}; pooled over 301 discharges the
\Ti{} skill over the causal GP is $+0.057$ $[+0.027, +0.085]$ at 20\,ms, $+0.104$
$[+0.079, +0.128]$ at 50\,ms and $+0.143$ $[+0.118, +0.168]$ at 630\,ms (four-split
means $+0.055$, $+0.098$ and $+0.138$), every interval excluding zero, with the
per-discharge win rate at 0.52, 0.64 and 0.67. One past observation and 50\,ms of
contiguous context are different resources, and the windowed family cannot supply the
second at any $W$ (its window is pooled without order and its unlabelled rows are
dropped): the $W{=}2$ control's skill over the causal GP is $+0.041$ (CI above zero
on 1/4 splits) and \seqv{} restricted to the same two steps has $+0.055$ (2/4). At
matched reach a recurrent LSTM (357{,}570 parameters), a dilated causal convolution
(3{,}238) and banded attention (295{,}746) have \Ti{} skill over the causal GP of
$+0.113$, $+0.119$ and $+0.119$ with the CI above zero on 4/4 splits; the largest
paired family difference is $-0.023$ (attention at the 70\,ms rung, CI excluding zero
on 3/4 splits), against $+0.060$ for moving reach from 20 to 70\,ms, and a diagonal
state-space model reaches $+0.105$ at 630\,ms against the recurrent $+0.143$ (pooled).
Online single-step cost follows the number of dispatched operators (about
2--3\,$\mu$s each): 111 per step for the LSTM at any reach, 209--305 for the dilated
convolution and 473 for banded attention at reach 15--63, so the architecture is
chosen on cost and not on skill; measured as the network forward pass only (1{,}000
timed calls at batch 1 after warm-up, laptop-class machine), the stateful \seqv{}
step costs \textbf{0.97\,ms median and 1.49\,ms at p99 on CPU} (0.51--1.05\,ms median
in earlier runs of the same benchmark), which is the basis for calling it usable
inside a 10\,ms cycle.

\paragraph{The model's per-discharge skill is positive where the target moves.}
On the same context ladder the pooled \Vrot{} skill at 70\,ms is $+0.123$
$[+0.036, +0.248]$, excluding zero, but the per-discharge win rate is 0.48 and
removing the top five of some 62 discharges takes the pooled skill to zero or below
on all four splits (\Ti{}: win rate 0.70, largest single contributor 9--16\%), and of
eleven covariates tested the one that predicts a positive per-discharge skill is how
much the target moves within a discharge: by tercile of that spread the win rate is
42\% / 83\% / 85\% for \Ti{} and 34\% / 48\% / 55\% for \Vrot{}.

% =========================================================================
\section{Where the remaining headroom is}
\label{sec:headroom}

The negative results in this paper are unusually specific, and specificity is what
makes them useful: they do not say ``this problem is hard'', they say \emph{which
change would move it}. Capacity is ruled out (\S\ref{sec:ladder}), longer windows
are ruled out (\S\ref{sec:context}), inductive bias, cross-device pretraining and
ensembling are ruled out (\S\ref{sec:ladder}), and the framing that buys reach has
been adopted (\S\ref{sec:gate}). The one model-side axis that moved is the loss's
influence function, and its gain is a bulk gain (\S\ref{sec:bulk}). What remains
beyond that is data, and each lever is identified by evidence already in this
dataset.

\paragraph{1. CES fit-quality metadata would replace a proxy with a measurement.}
The two-population report exists because a value cut is a proxy for ``the fit
failed'': it removes one-sample upward events that no method can predict, but it
is one-sided (dips are untouched) and it catches only 19\% of $\geq 2\times$
upward outliers (\S\ref{sec:spikes}). With per-sample fit $\chi^2$ or signal
level, a quality cut would replace or accompany the value cut in every arm at
once, and the two populations would collapse into one. The route to those
values already exists on the same device: NN-CES analyses CES spectra without
beam modulation and so yields a fit diagnostic per
exposure~\citep{Lee2026NeuralNetworkbased}, which also removes the gaps that come
from modulation itself. This lever is a CES reanalysis product, not a code change
on our side. \Vrot{}'s own spikes
(119 rows above 1{,}000\,km/s) would be handled by the same rule; until then any
persistence-anchored \Vrot{} comparison reports the share of squared error those
rows carry, as \S\ref{sec:ladder} does.

\paragraph{2. The raw Mirnov stream was tested: the registered features do not carry
\Vrot{}.} On the identical 10\,ms grid, lag-1 autocorrelation
within contiguous blocks is $+0.568$ for BES and $+0.572$ for ECEI but $-0.009$ for
the Mirnov coils, with 82\% of blocks below $|r| = 0.1$: the magnetic channel is
white noise \emph{on this grid}. That is the signature of $\mathrm{d}B/\mathrm{d}t$
oscillating at the kHz mode frequency and being decimated to 100\,Hz without an
anti-aliasing filter, so successive samples have random relative phase. The
mode-rotation frequency---the one quantity in our diagnostic set that could proxy
toroidal rotation---was therefore discarded upstream of the model, which is also why
every derived MC feature we tried (integral, PCHIP integral, $|MC|$, rolling RMS)
failed: information already lost cannot be recovered downstream. That reading named
a preprocessing fix, and the fix was tested under a pre-registration. The raw
2\,MHz coil stream was obtained for 12 discharges. It first turns the decimation
reading into a measurement: on 24 of 24 coils checked, the 100\,Hz value in the shot
files equals a single raw sample at the grid time (lag 0, difference zero or within
the print quantum), that is, a point snapshot with no averaging and no filter. Then
15 causal 10\,ms window
features (RMS envelope and five band powers per coil, and the dominant peak of the
two-coil cross-spectrum) were routed into the \Vrot{} branch, with six training
discharges and three \Vrot{}-carrying test discharges. The paired change in \Vrot{}
skill is $-0.128$ $[-0.544, -0.105]$ in the cut population and $-0.164$
$[-0.473, -0.133]$ in the inclusive one. Both intervals exclude zero on the negative
side, and 0 of 3 test discharges improve. The coil physics itself is confirmed: the
edge harmonic oscillation of \#32092 appears at 4.39 and 8.91\,kHz. But the dominant
mode frequency in a 10\,ms window is not a row-by-row function of the CES edge
rotation: its within-discharge Spearman correlation with \Vrot{} is $|\rho| \leq 0.11$
in six of seven discharges. The rejection covers the 15 registered features on a
six-discharge training set. Other functions of the raw stream (for example the
cross-phase slope over many coils) were not tested. Raw Mirnov features are
therefore not a named next experiment for the 10\,ms \Vrot{} nowcast.

\paragraph{3. The actuator channel is absent, and at 10\,ms it would change little.}
Toroidal rotation is set by injected torque, and no torque signal exists in this
dataset. The data show the break precisely: between shots, the ECE-derived $T_e$
surrogate correlates with \Ti{} at $r = +0.353$ ($p = 3\times10^{-17}$) but with
\Vrot{} at $r = +0.024$ ($p = 0.58$), and within shots the \Ti{} correlation keeps a
consistent sign while the \Vrot{} one is sign-random. So $T_e$ does track the heating
level, and heating level does not reach rotation---power is not torque, which depends
on beam energy, tangency radius and injection geometry. NBI torque is the cause of
the rotation \emph{level}. It is not a lever for the 10\,ms nowcast. Beam power is
a step input, held constant between a handful of source on/off steps per
discharge, so it acts only on the slow band. The part of the 10\,ms increment
variance carried by a 300\,ms moving average is 0.34\% for \Vrot{} (interquartile
range 0.21--0.94\%, 20 discharges) and 0.25\% for \Ti{} (63 discharges). A perfect
torque channel therefore bounds the removable 10\,ms increment variance at about
1\%, and the level it sets is already in the input as the value observed 10\,ms
earlier. The channel matters for a different scope: forecasts of 100\,ms and longer
after a power step, and the cold start before the first CES sample. The positive
control in the literature is of that kind: recurrent full-discharge simulators on
DIII-D that receive the beam actuators as inputs predict rotation's
evolution~\citep{Char2024FullShot}.

\paragraph{4. The rest of the bulk belongs to the future neighbour.}
After the Huber arm's recovery, a 4\,eV median gap to PCHIP remains
(\S\ref{sec:bulk}). Its size is what averaging two adjacent noisy observations buys,
so the only way a causal model closes it is by denoising the history---weighting it
by the per-exposure fit quality a CES re-analysis would provide---which is the same
deliverable as lever 1. And the zero-label row of the model-family card
(\S\ref{sec:ladder}) shows the cold-start scope of item 3: with no same-shot \Vrot{}
label, no learned arm rises above the training mean from BES, ECEI and Mirnov alone.

For the 10\,ms nowcast the lever that remains is therefore the per-exposure fit
quality of items 1 and 4, which the 641 shot files do not contain. Item 2 is a
route closed within its registered scope, and item 3 belongs to forecasts of
100\,ms and longer.

% =========================================================================
\section{Limitations}
\label{sec:limits}

\textbf{The headline skill is a tail statistic.} In the median row the backbone
equals persistence and trails PCHIP by 20\%, and \Vrot{} is below persistence in the
median (\S\ref{sec:bulk}); the paper therefore reports median absolute error beside
every aggregate skill and does not claim a lower error than interpolation on a typical row. The
scale-pinned Huber loss recovers 8--10\% of the bulk at no aggregate cost
(13\% when selected on its own objective), reported as conditional on the cut
population; the same rule lifts the inclusive median gain to $+0.285$ but leaves
one split with an MSE difference of $-0.040$ whose CI is below zero, which a longer cap does not remove
(\S\ref{sec:bulk}). The
\Ti{} median is owned by a physics filter unconditionally (\S\ref{sec:physfilter}),
reported beside, not inside, the aggregate model; for \Vrot{} that filter's median-error
ratio to persistence is 0.94--1.00 with the interval including 1 on 3/4 splits, at the
photon floor of the 10\,ms line fit.
\textbf{Statistical power.} The unit of replication is the shot; with 96 (\Ti) /
60--66 (\Vrot) test shots per split, power bounds every significance call, and
per-shot squared-error differences are heavy-tailed (a few discharges dominate the
bootstrap spread; in the inclusive population $\approx$1\% of rows carry 70--83\%
of every arm's \Ti{} squared error).
\textbf{MNAR optimism.} Skill is measured on observed points only; the reweighting
of \S\ref{sec:mnar} bounds the optimism for the causal comparison in both
populations and for the offline comparison with population-conditional
significance, and it covers 54--68\% of missing \Ti{} rows and 4--6\% of missing
\Vrot{} rows.
\textbf{The offline claim is bounded above by the offline GP.} The offline GP's
\Ti{} RMSE is below PCHIP's (153.8 vs.\ 173.6) and the model's paired skill against
it is $-0.05$ to $+0.11$ with the CI including zero on 7/8 cells, so ``skill over
future-using interpolation'' means ``skill over the pre-registered interpolants'';
it does not extend to every offline method. It does extend to the causal GP, the
strongest deployable one ($+0.08$ to $+0.17$, CIs above zero on 8/8).
\textbf{The value cut is a proxy.} Two populations bracket the fit-failure
question; a fit-quality cut would settle it (\S\ref{sec:headroom}), and \Vrot{}'s
spikes remain uncut.
\textbf{Campaign transfer rests on one temporal block} (\S\ref{sec:campaign}):
four initialisations, not four splits, and 2/4 cut-population runs stopped at the
epoch cap. The repair that makes the windowed control transfer, per-shot
standardization, is the offline form; a causal running (expanding-window/EWMA)
estimator is the version that would ship and is not measured here.
\textbf{Metric asymmetry.} Interpolants use full-shot neighbours while the
windowed control sees two rows and the backbone the segment's past; this is
deliberately adverse to the causal models but complicates direct interpretation.
\textbf{Single device and model family.} Everything is one device, one diagnostic
set and two closely related recurrent families; nothing here establishes transfer
to another tokamak.
\textbf{Uncertainty is calibrated on pooled rows.} The coverage of the predictive
head is reported per split over all rows (\S\ref{sec:dist}); its coverage per
discharge was not measured.
\textbf{Latency} is a network-only measurement on one laptop-class machine, with
up to 2$\times$ run-to-run variation from power states (\S\ref{sec:context});
feature assembly and acquisition overhead are not included.
\textbf{Scope.} The pedestal-top framing is inherited from the data selection
(pedestal-top CES channels); no radial-dependence experiment is performed, and
event-phase analyses (ELM cycle, L--H transitions) are future work---the
high-variability analysis of \S\ref{sec:peak} is an event-agnostic proxy.
\textbf{Scope of the asymmetry.} The \Ti$\leftrightarrow$\Vrot{} statement holds for
standard CES at 10\,ms, from the core to the pedestal top, with the NBI torque
unobserved; edge $E_r$ and rotation are known to move within an ELM
cycle~\citep{Viezzer2020Dynamics,Cavedon2017Pedestal}, and a measurement that resolves
the ELM cycle could carry fast-channel information about rotation that ours cannot.
\textbf{The equation is three quarters of the backbone, read in one population.}
22--28\% of the backbone's PCHIP-relative skill is nonlinear event handling that the
20-parameter form does not reproduce, and its physical bands are read from the cut
population only: in the inclusive population the equation keeps 0.43--0.81 of the
PCHIP-relative skill and its BES gain changes sign under the fit-failure spikes
(\S\ref{sec:model:backbone}).

% =========================================================================
\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

A missing 10\,ms CES row in KSTAR can be filled by a strictly causal estimator with
lower mean-squared error than by interpolation that reads the future, for ion
temperature and for rotation; what separates the two quantities is what the fast
diagnostics contain. We built that estimator---a full-grid two-branch causal LSTM whose \Vrot{}
branch never sees the fast diagnostics---and evaluated it under a pre-registered,
shot-clustered, two-population protocol against a deliberately adverse bar:
interpolation that sees the future, and a causal GP that is the strongest method that
does not. The model's skill over future-using PCHIP for ion temperature is $+0.17$ to
$+0.32$ across four independent splits and both populations with every interval
excluding zero ($[+0.19, +0.25]$ and $[+0.19, +0.31]$ under a pre-registered repeated
5-fold replicate that tests every discharge once), its paired skill against the
strongest offline smoother is $-0.05$ to $+0.11$ with the interval including zero on
7/8 cells, and its skill over the causal GP is $+0.08$ to $+0.17$ with the interval
above zero on all eight cells (and $+0.27$ and $+0.21$ in the non-adjacent regime,
$\Delta t > 15$\,ms). The skill survives both stress tests: at genuinely missing,
in-domain timesteps the skill over persistence stays at $+0.28$ to $+0.44$ with
intervals above zero on 8/8 cells, and across a campaign boundary the sequence
nowcaster keeps $+0.17$ to $+0.20$ over PCHIP and $+0.11$ to $+0.16$ over the causal
GP with intervals above zero on 4/4 initialisations, where the windowed control it
replaced had lost its offline advantage (interval above zero on 2/4 and 0/4 vs.\
PCHIP)---the fast diagnostics drift 5--11$\times$ more between campaigns than the
targets, and the sequence framing standardizes per shot and reaches the whole past
by construction.

What that nowcaster computes can be written down. Weight magnitude told us nothing
stable; the input--output response did, and a four-stage registered readout turned it
into a 20-parameter physical filter: an observation filter whose gain on a new
measurement rises with the gap since the last one, plus a linear response to each
fast channel's deviation from its preceding 100\,ms baseline that is switched off
beyond a learned threshold. Trained from scratch under the identical protocol, that
equation keeps 72--78\% of the backbone's PCHIP-relative skill on 4/4 cut splits,
above the registered 0.70 bar. The remainder is the network's nonlinear event
handling; it is the price of a 20-parameter description, not a missing term that
these inputs expose. The bulk of the skill is denoising of the noisy anchor, and the
margin over interpolation is carried by the rows where a pedestal event is seen in
BES and ECEI before the next CES exposure.

Rotation also has a lower mean error, from a different source. Its skill over
PCHIP under the registered two-level bootstrap over eight new partitions is
$[+0.07, +0.70]$ (cut) and $[+0.05, +0.68]$ (inclusive), excluding zero, and it is
carried by the CES history alone: the fast channels correlate with $d\Vrot/dt$ at
$-0.006$ and $-0.003$ against $+0.070$ and $+0.078$ with $d\Ti/dt$
(\S\ref{sec:model:physics}), the 100\,Hz Mirnov values are single raw samples, and
registered features of the raw 2\,MHz stream change the skill by $-0.128$
$[-0.544, -0.105]$ (cut; three test discharges; \S\ref{sec:headroom}). The aggregate
skill of both targets is a tail statistic---in the median row the nowcaster equals
persistence for \Ti{} and is worse than it for \Vrot{} (4.3 vs 3.7\,km/s,
\S\ref{sec:bulk})---so the median comes from a separate estimator: a pre-registered
hold-or-jump filter with Student-$t$ noise reaches 0.91--0.92$\times$ persistence for \Ti{}
on 8/8 cells, while for \Vrot{} the interval of its error ratio includes 1 on 3/4
splits, which is the photon floor of a 10\,ms line fit. A Student-$t$
distribution head carries the calibrated uncertainty (\S\ref{sec:dist}). The
statement is scoped to standard CES at 10\,ms from the core to the pedestal top; edge
rotation inside an ELM cycle is a different measurement.

We also report what is not claimed and what would overturn it. The offline claim is
bounded above by the offline GP; the value cut that defines one population is a
one-sided proxy for fit quality, and CES fit-quality metadata would replace it; the
reweighting reaches 54--68\% of missing \Ti{} rows and a twentieth of missing \Vrot{}
rows; the predictive intervals are calibrated on pooled rows, and per-discharge coverage was not measured; beyond
45\,ms the inclusive-population interval includes zero ($-0.004$, $[-0.30, +0.25]$);
the equation's physical bands are read from the cut population only, since under the
fit-failure spikes its inclusive BES gain changes sign; and everything is one device
and one campaign. The model-size and model-family axes are closed---a 21k-parameter
persistence-plus-bounded-correction model matches the backbone under the cut, a
26$\times$ width sweep is flat, and a shot-encoding neural process, a transformer
pretrained on another tokamak and a 4-init ensemble change \Ti{} skill by $-0.09$ to
$+0.03$ with none clearing the 0.02 band in both populations---so what
remains is on the input side: per-exposure fit uncertainty from the CES analysis for
the 10\,ms nowcast, and the NBI torque channel only for forecasts of 100\,ms and
longer: beam power is a step input, and the band carried by a 300\,ms moving average
holds 0.34\% of the 10\,ms \Vrot{} increment variance (\S\ref{sec:headroom}). The evaluation that supports all
of this---pre-registration with a scored prediction ledger, discharge-cluster
intervals, overlap-corrected repeated cross-validation and a two-level
bootstrap---is assembled from standard pieces of other fields; we found no precedent
for the combination in peer-reviewed fusion machine learning (\S\ref{sec:related}),
and it is reported as the condition of belief, not as a result.

% =========================================================================
\subsubsection*{Reproducibility}
Splits are pinned to disk and verified on reload; normalization statistics are
train-file-only (plus per-shot input standardization for the sequence family);
model selection never reads test data; bootstrap uses a fixed seed and 10{,}000
resamples; every quoted number is read from frozen evaluation artifacts by one
collection script.

\subsubsection*{Code availability}
The full pipeline, the pre-registration document with its per-batch execution
records, the controlled-experiment runners behind every result reported here, the
pinned train/validation/test splits, and the collector that regenerates every
quoted number from the frozen evaluation artifacts are openly available at
\url{https://github.com/iseungsang01/ml-intern-revision}. The backbone is
\texttt{ces\_prediction/experiments/seq/model\_seq\_v2.py}, the interpretable rung
\texttt{model\_seq\_b3.py}, and the windowed control
\texttt{ces\_prediction/model\_iter009.py} (guarded by a content hash in the test
suite), so the code that produced these numbers cannot drift from the code that is
released.
% TODO(user): mint an archival DOI (e.g. Zenodo) for the submitted revision and cite it here.

\subsubsection*{Data availability}
The KSTAR diagnostic data underlying this study --- 641 discharges, shots
30801--32751 --- are not redistributed with the code. They are experimental data of
the KSTAR device and are governed by the operating institution's data policy;
access requests should be directed there. The repository contains everything needed
to reproduce the analysis once the shot files are in place: the exact file-level
split manifests, the environment configuration for every reported run, and the
per-sample squared-error archives from which the bootstrap statistics are computed.
